Name: Ananias of Damascus
Summary: Ananias was a devout disciple at Damascus whom the Lord sent to the blinded Saul after the Damascus road. He laid hands on Saul, who regained his sight and was baptised, and later defended Ananias' character before the Jerusalem crowd.
KeyStory: Ananias, who feared Saul's reputation, obeyed and called the persecutor brother, and Saul rose baptised.
LifeLesson: Obedience to a frightening assignment can open a persecutor's eyes. Ananias went, and Paul began.
